messages:
apexbio_ops: Hey team, our Private Redwood endpoint in us-east-1 started returning 502s and deploys are failing around 09:10 UTC. Errors look like TLS handshake failures from the client side. No config changes on our app, but we did touch egress ACLs last night. Can someone check peering/VPN?

maria_s: sorry to hear that — opening an escalation. @network_oncall can you take a look? Can apexbio share quick repro/traces? :mag_right:

network_oncall: I'm seeing intermittent drops on the IPsec tunnels to ApexBio. Control plane reachability is flapping between UDP/4500 and ESP (proto 50) behavior. Can you run a tcpdump on your appliance: `sudo tcpdump -n -i <iface> port 4500 or proto 50` and paste few lines?

apexbio_ops: attaching a short tcpdump snippet from their edge (trimmed):
```
09:09:58.123456 IP 198.51.100.21.4500 > 10.0.0.5.4500: UDP, length 128
09:09:58.223789 IP 10.0.0.5.4500 > 198.51.100.21.4500: UDP, length 128
09:10:02.000000 IP 198.51.100.21 > 10.0.0.5: ESP(spi=0x5f3a2b)
09:10:02.000100 IP 10.0.0.5 > 198.51.100.21: ICMP 10.0.0.5 udp port 4500 unreachable, length 36
09:10:05.500000 IP 198.51.100.21.4500 > 10.0.0.5.4500: UDP, length 64 (retrans)
```

apexbio_ops: also seeing TLS errors in our proxy: `tls: remote error: handshake failure` and connection reset in the app logs.

devops_eli: fwiw our side shows `tls: server name "private.cp.redwood.internal" mismatch` occasionally, and some conn resets. Could be a middlebox doing TLS interception or SNI rewriting.

maria_s: did you change any egress allowlist or enable a TLS inspection proxy recently? That would explain both UDP/ESP issues and TLS errors.

apexbio_ops: we did tighten egress last night — outgoing UDP ephemeral ports were mostly blocked except 4500, and we added a transparent TLS proxy for inspection on port 443 for some infra teams.

network_oncall: that aligns with what I'm seeing. NAT-T needs UDP 4500, but some implementations also use ephemeral UDP ports for keepalives and resiliency; if those are blocked the tunnel can switch modes or fail. If ESP (proto 50) is blocked by a firewall then the peer might be trying ESP and getting dropped (ICMP unreachable seen). Also TLS interception can break mutual TLS/SNI used by the control plane.

infra_bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1438 (private-peering-apexbio). Assigned to networking + support.

maria_s: proposed remediation steps:
1) Temporarily allow IP proto 50 (ESP) and ephemeral UDP (>1024) egress to Redwood peer IP ranges while we validate.
2) Disable the transparent TLS proxy for traffic to `*.redwood.internal` (or add an allow rule to bypass inspection).
3) Collect `sudo ipsec statusall` and `/var/log/auth.log | grep -i strongswan` for 09:00-09:15 and paste here.

network_oncall: sharing `ipsec status` from our side (truncated):
```
Security Associations (1 up, 0 connecting):
  apexbio-redwood[1]: ESTABLISHED 3 minutes ago, 198.51.100.21[198.51.100.21]...10.0.0.5[10.0.0.5]
    AES_CBC_256/HMAC_SHA1_96/PRF_HMAC_SHA1/MODP2048
    spi=0x5f3a2b9a(159...): reqid=1 mode=Tunnel, encap=yes (UDP)
    packets: recv 102 tx 98 errors 12
    rekeying never
```

network_oncall: note `errors 12` and encap=yes indicates NAT-T. Counters increment when UDP/4500 packets are dropped — that matches the tcpdump ICMP unreachable.

apexbio_ops: we temporarily allowed ESP + ephemeral UDP and turned off TLS proxy bypass for `*.redwood.internal`. After 2 minutes we retried deploy and the 502s stopped. API requests to the private endpoint now succeed.

apexbio_ops: confirmed stable for 10m, rolling back monitoring shows no TLS handshake errors. Thanks! :tada:

maria_s: great — next steps: please keep the allowlist changes in place while we coordinate a permanent recommendation. We'll update the Private VPC docs to call out required egress: UDP 4500, ephemeral UDP ports, and IP proto 50 (ESP), plus an exception for TLS inspection on Redwood internal hostnames.

network_oncall: I'll file a doc PR and add a checklist for onboarding Private customers (include packet capture commands, ipsec status examples, and firewall rules).

devops_eli: saving tcpdump/ipsec snippets to the incident ticket for postmortem.

apexbio_ops: appreciate the fast response. If anything else pops up we'll ping INC-2026-1438.

infra_bot: INC-2026-1438 status -> mitigated (temporary config change by customer).

maria_s: marking as resolved after docs PR and confirm with customer later today. Thanks everyone.
